state.context:
Assess a canonical body spelling for canlang scenarios from three candidates. This AI-authored CRUD SaaS DSL targets adoption through concise tokens, consistent generation and simple primitives. No executable compiler/runtime or empirically measured token, generation or maintenance outcomes are available. Semantic familiarity is a hypothesis about agents rather than an observed advantage.
Scenario declarations retain typed inputs and distinguish user by from trusted on. Currently then can open nested statements or prefix simple semicolon-separated ones. Validation occurs on either side: 254 markers consist of 154 standalone and 100 inline uses, with 34 requires inside their blocks. Nesting uses one space. Failed checks roll back a whole provisional mutation regardless of position, and the marker itself does not establish atomicity. Read scenarios remain pure and require a typed result. Uppercase Given/When/Then survives with Then governing presentation, and actual test observations belong to attached test-only examples. # annotations and ## comments are unchanged.
Renaming to do changes only the word, retaining body boundaries, forms, action/check order, lexical names, authorization and test attachment. Its execution association could distinguish body code from BDD observations; it could also sound unnecessarily effectful for read-only code and demand a new learned spelling. It saves 508 UTF-8 bytes over 254 markers, with zero line/depth reduction and unknown tokenizer effect. Retaining then needs no spelling migration and maintains an existing explicit body delimiter, while retaining potential result/sequence and uppercase/BDD connotation overlap. Omitting the container gives direct ordered children, moving its subtree out once; this avoids 154 container lines and repeated words but needs careful nesting migration and a clearly reserved examples boundary. Required expressiveness and semantics must survive whichever design is chosen; no sample proves equivalence. None supplies new atomicity or authority. These are competing canonical choices, not multiple supported forms.
Illustrative models and fixtures show structural differences without a compiled program. Include costs as well as gains and retain uncertainty when comparative support is thin. Prior classifier results and a consensus forecast are absent from the evidence.

examples.then_body:
scenario finish(item:Item) by=members
 require item.status==open
 then
  let selected=item.Part
  require count(selected)>0
  set item {status=done}
 examples item=fixture_item
  item.status -> item.status
  open -> done
examples.do_body:
scenario finish(item:Item) by=members
 require item.status==open
 do
  let selected=item.Part
  require count(selected)>0
  set item {status=done}
 examples item=fixture_item
  item.status -> item.status
  open -> done
examples.direct_body:
scenario finish(item:Item) by=members
 require item.status==open
 let selected=item.Part
 require count(selected)>0
 set item {status=done}
 examples item=fixture_item
  item.status -> item.status
  open -> done

body_spelling.instructions: Taking these product aims and competing consequences together, which notation should define scenario bodies?

criteria.do: Adopt do in place of then, preserving the existing container boundaries and semantics.
criteria.then: Preserve the present lowercase then body marker and its current forms.
criteria.unresolved: Withhold a preferred notation because comparative support is insufficient.
criteria.direct: Drop the extra marker and order executable children directly inside each scenario.
